issues.description: Method PersonService.getAllPersons has inconsistent return types across artifacts: the problem statement and the template/server stub define/getAllPersons as returning a List<Person>, and the client code (PersonController) expects a List<Person> (it calls WebClient and deserializes to a List). In the solution implementation, PersonService.getAllPersons is implemented to return Set<Person>. Furthermore, PersonResource in the solution declares the controller method as ResponseEntity<List<Person>> but returns ResponseEntity.ok(personService.getAllPersons(...)) where personService.getAllPersons(...) yields a Set<Person>, causing a generic type mismatch and a compilation error. This inconsistency will prevent the server code from compiling and confuses students about whether the API should return a List or a Set.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across specification, server service, resource, and client. Preferred fix: change PersonService.getAllPersons to return List<Person> (signature: public List<Person> getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions sortingOptions)) and return a sorted List (e.g., new ArrayList<>(sortedList) or Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedList)). Update the solution implementation accordingly and ensure PersonResource passes that List to ResponseEntity.ok(...) and the client continues to use ParameterizedTypeReference<List<Person>>. Alternatively, if a Set is intentionally desired, update the problem statement, PersonResource return type, and the client deserialization to use Set<Person> consistently, but the safer choice to match the documented API is to return List<Person>.
